claims.text: The initial high-entropy alloy is a single-phase solid solution.
Mechanical loading causes nano-scale precipitates to form in the alloy.
Mechanical loading produces dislocation pile-ups in the alloy.
Nano-scale precipitates act as stress concentrators.
Dislocation pile-ups act as stress concentrators.
Stress concentrations associated with precipitates and dislocation pile-ups facilitate crack initiation.
Stress concentrations associated with precipitates and dislocation pile-ups facilitate crack propagation.
The proposed mechanism causes loss of toughness or brittle fracture under mechanical loading.
The alloy will exhibit a 20% decrease in toughness relative to its initial baseline.
The alloy will exhibit a 30% increase in brittle-fracture probability relative to its initial baseline.
The proposed in situ straining test uses a strain rate of 10^-4 s^-1 and a maximum strain of 10%.
The proposed test is conducted at room temperature and atmospheric pressure.
The stated service boundary applies at strain rates above 10^-3 s^-1.
The stated service boundary applies at temperatures above 500°C.
Grain-boundary segregation may influence the fracture outcome.
Dynamic recrystallization during deformation may influence the fracture outcome.
A 10% increase in toughness together with a 20% decrease in brittle-fracture probability under the same loading conditions would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The experiment uses 10^-4 s^-1, whereas the stated applicable boundary is above 10^-3 s^-1, so the proposed test lies outside the claimed strain-rate regime.
The experiment is conducted at room temperature, whereas the stated applicable boundary is above 500°C, so the proposed test does not probe the claimed temperature regime.
